ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against Global Affairs Canada's consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the US OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists for USD clearing transactions, and United Kingdom consolidated sanctions lists where applicable. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all foreign politically exposed persons, domestic PEPs, and family members or close associates thereof, following FINTRAC interpretive guidance and FATF standards. Final screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in Alberta must be in English or French or a combination of both. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet and approved by the Alberta Corporate Registry. A permissible corporate suffix such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., or the French equivalents must be included.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the refusal, including the NUANS search report, proposed name, and any third-party consents or explanatory submissions. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within the applicable statutory appeal period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for a single-family office only where there is a physical registered office in Alberta capable of receiving service of process and where corporate records and accounting records are available at a physical address in the province. Purely mail-forwarding arrangements or P.O. Box addresses are not compliant with Alberta Business Corporations Act requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for a passive private investment holding entity; approximate annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry, FINTRAC, or the Canada Revenue Agency is 5-10%, increasing to approximately 15% in the presence of PEP or material enhanced-due-diligence triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended: s. 6 (general powers of incorporation), s. 10 (contents of articles), s. 12 (effective date of incorporation), s. 25 (form of consideration for shares), s. 100 (registered office), s. 101 (records office), s. 106 (first directors), s. 9 (correction of articles).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (operating the Corporate Registry System and supervising accredited service providers)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), together with Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office Address) and Form 3 (Notice of First Directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under Alberta law; a corporation may be incorporated with nil issued capital and shares may be issued for money, property or past services (s. 25 ABCA). No escrow account or capital contribution deposit requirement applies to a standard private business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Be it resolved: (1) Share Subscriptions – The subscriptions contained in the Articles of Incorporation are accepted; the Corporation shall allot and issue the subscribed common shares against the agreed consideration, and the Secretary shall arrange share certificates per the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). (2) Registered Office – The Corporation's registered office and records office are established at the address in the Notice of Registered Office Address. (3) Officers – The Board appoints [President], [Secretary], and [Treasurer] to serve until the first annual meeting or earlier removal. The officers are authorized to execute banking, custody, and regulatory filings for the Corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Availability Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via accredited NUANS service providers (corporate-registry.alberta.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search (NUANS) request through an accredited service provider, providing the proposed corporate legal name, the jurisdiction of activity, and the desired corporate designation (Ltd., Inc., Corp., or ULC). Obtain the NUANS report, which must be submitted together with the Articles of Incorporation to establish name distinctiveness and compliance with the Alberta Business Corporations Act name requirements.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate legal name (English/French)
Corporate designation suffix (Ltd., Inc., Corp., ULC)
Completed NUANS name search request form
Prescribed name search fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or marked as conflicting, file a fresh NUANS request with an alternate proposed name, or obtain the written consent of the holder of the conflicting name and submit that consent with the amended filing; the name can also be abandoned in favour of a numbered incorporation where distinctiveness cannot be established.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (online filing through Corporate Registry System or accredited service providers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) specifying the corporate name, share structure and classes, any restrictions on share transfers or business purposes, and the maximum or minimum number of directors. Each incorporator must sign the articles. File the executed Form 1 together with the NUANS report, Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office Address), Form 3 (Notice of First Directors), and the prescribed registry fee. Upon approval, the registry endorses the articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence that the corporation is duly incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation signed by each incorporator
NUANS Name Search Report
Form 2 – Notice of Registered Office Address
Form 3 – Notice of First Directors
Payment of applicable filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns the package for correction under s. 9 ABCA, cure the stated deficiencies by preparing corrected articles, resubmitting the corrected Form 1 with the amendment fee, and ensuring consistent information on Forms 2 and 3; incorporation takes effect on the date the corrected articles are endorsed and the Certificate of Incorporation is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number Registration and Corporate Tax Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) portal (cra-arc.gc.ca / bro.cra-arc.gc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated Alberta corporation with the CRA through the Business Registration Online portal or Form RC 1 to obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and the corporation's Corporate Income Tax program account (RT). Because Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA, the RT account also covers Alberta provincial corporate tax. For a single family office conducting passive investment holding, a GST/HST account is generally unnecessary unless taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold; the operator should confirm whether any GST/HST election applies.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Alberta)
Alberta Corporate Registry file number
Description of principal business activity (NAICS 525920 – Private Investment Holding)
Name, address and identification of the directing mind of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects or questions the program account application, correct the data through the BRO portal, or contact the CRA business tax line for a manual amendment; no late-filing penalty accrues provided the registration is completed before the first corporate income tax return filing due date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Corporate Tax Confirmation and Annual Registry Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance (provincial corporate tax, administered via CRA); Alberta Corporate Registry for annual returns
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the corporate income tax program account effective date and filing calendar with the CRA for Alberta corporate income tax purposes. Access the Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) system to establish the annual return obligation: the annual return is due within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation, with prescribed fees. For a single family office, confirm that the registered office and directors' records are current, as the annual return requires naming the directors and confirming the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and registry file number
CRA RT account confirmation
Proof of registered office address (lease or utility record)
Current director information for the annual return
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is missed, file the late annual return promptly with the arrears fee and, if the corporation has been administratively dissolved, seek voluntary reinstatement under s. 118 ABCA within the cure periods; the registry will restore the corporation upon payment of all arrears and reinstatement fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Private Banking and Securities Custody Account Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank or trust company licensed in Alberta (private banking and securities custody division)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporation's operating account and institutional securities custody account with a private banking counterparty, presenting the corporate authorization package: Certificate of Incorporation, formation board resolution, corporate register (shareholders, directors and officers), registered office A-memorandum, and the family office beneficial ownership and KYC/AML documentation. Execute the account opening agreements, designate officer signing authorities, and establish wire transfer and reporting protocols consistent with the target payment rails: Private Banking Wire and Securities Custody.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (red ribbon or certified copy)
First Board Resolution containing officer appointments
Corporate register of shareholders, directors and officers (certified extract)
Registered office address confirmation letter
Beneficial owner identification, KYC/AML documentation and source of funds evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution questions the signing authority or beneficial ownership structure, issue a fresh certified extract of the register of directors and a ratified board resolution confirming the appointed officers and designated banking signatories; the bank may also require updated beneficial owner declarations to satisfy Canadian AML/KYC obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – office-based single family office investment holding entity; no industrial plant or manufacturing facility within the scope of Alberta industrial licensing (Alberta Municipal Affairs / municipal business licensing at place of registered office)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no manufacturing or industrial operating permit required; a municipal office business licence (if imposed by the host municipality, e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence) and a valid leasehold occupancy clearance suffice for the administrative investment-holding activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the single family office performs purely administrative investment-holding functions with no physical project, construction, or operational facility; no Environmental Impact Assessment is required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-3, and no registration or approval is triggered for office-only premises
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or atmospheric emissions are generated; office premises must comply with municipal wastewater and solid waste management bylaws, landlord building operational standards, and applicable indoor air quality and safe occupancy thresholds for administrative space

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for office occupancy under the Alberta Fire Code (Alberta Regulation 31/2021); occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 and the OHS Code, including general workplace safety, emergency preparedness and fire escape inspections; leasehold certificate of occupancy confirming structural load limits are appropriate for administrative use with no industrial racking or heavy load operations

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - federal Part I corporate income tax, GST/HST, Part XIII withholding and, under the 2008 Alberta Tax Administration Agreement, Alberta provincial corporate income tax is assessed, collected and administered by CRA. Registration and filing portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/canada-revenue-agency-digital-services-businesses.html); Alberta corporate registry: Alberta Corporate Registration System (ACRS), Service Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate in Alberta under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) via ACRS, or federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act followed by extra-provincial registration in Alberta; the registration generates a Corporate Access Number. Step 2: CRA normally issues the 9-digit Business Number (BN) automatically upon incorporation through the Newly Incorporated Business stream; if not, file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or register online. Step 3: A non-resident corporation must provide proof of continued existence (foreign certificate of good standing), designate a Canadian representative/address for service, and, if applying for a GST/HST account, an authorized Canadian agent for records purposes under ETA subsection 286(2.1). Step 4: Activate relevant program accounts under the BN: GST/HST (RT) only when worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 (four-quarter small-supplier test) or voluntarily to support zero-rating of exports; payroll (RP) if employees are engaged; income tax (RC) for Part XIII withholding on non-resident payments. For a Single Family Office earning primarily exempt financial supplies, GST registration is generally not required and is usually detrimental because ITCs are unavailable. Step 5: No Alberta corporate tax ID or separate provincial sales tax registration is required; Alberta has no PST and Alberta corporate income tax is reported through the federal T2 return using the same BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation with residence-based worldwide taxation; no pass-through eligibility for a Canadian business corporation. A Canadian-resident corporation is taxable under ITA subsection 2(2) and section 248(1) on worldwide income. Alberta general corporate rate: 8%; federal general rate: 15%; combined active business rate: 23%. For a Canadian-controlled private corporation earning aggregate investment income (the typical SFO HoldCo), the notional combined rate is approximately 46.7% (federal 38.67%, inclusive of 10% provincial abatement and 10.67% refundable top-up, plus Alberta 8%), of which approximately 30.7% is refundable through the Refundable Dividend Tax On Hand mechanism upon taxable dividend distributions, leaving an approximate net non-refundable burden of 16%. For a foreign-controlled (non-CCPC) holdco, the combined rate is 23%. Capital gains are subject to a one-half inclusion rate; eligible dividends are grossed up with a dividend tax credit at the shareholder level. No tax-exempt zone regime exists in Alberta; deferral for foreign subsidiaries is governed by the foreign accrual property income (FAPI) rules under ITA sections 91-95.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election; entity classification flows from corporate law, with CRA's Foreign Entity Classification rules (TIB-244R) governing hybrid foreign entities such as US LLCs. Available elections relevant to an SFO: (a) ITA section 85 rollover to transfer capital property into the corporation on a tax-deferred basis; (b) ITA section 83(2) capital dividend election to distribute tax-free Capital Dividend Account balances; (c) ITA section 89(1) paid-up capital elections; (d) ITA section 111(5.1) loss continuance election and section 111 loss carryover elections; (e) ETA section 150 election to treat closely related corporations as a single person for GST/HST (HoldCo + MgmtCo structures); (f) ETA section 156 election to deem supplies between closely related corporations to be for no consideration; (g) ITA section 216(4) election for non-resident owners of Canadian rental real estate held by the SFO; (h) ITA section 95(2)/(3) FAPI grouping and recharacterization elections for foreign affiliate structures; (i) ETA Part IX.1 election/designation as a selected listed financial institution where the SFO has permanent establishments in more than one province.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC); prudential supervisions by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); cross-border transaction surveillance and AML/CTF reporting administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), which oversees compliance with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada abolished all exchange control restrictions in 1952 (repeal of the Exchange Control Act) and operates a free-floating currency regime. There are no Central Bank approvals, registration requirements, or quotas for inbound or outbound capital remittances. Profit repatriation (dividends, interest, royalties, liquidation proceeds) is unrestricted, subject solely to federal Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25% domestic rate, reduced by applicable treaty, e.g., 5% under the Canada–US treaty on arm's-length dividends and 15% on portfolio dividends; subpart F/CBC thin-cap rules apply separately).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada has no export proceeds surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no timing constraints on retaining foreign currency. Exporters and holding entities may maintain foreign currency accounts domestically or offshore without restriction; only general reporting obligations apply, namely FINTRAC reports for cross-border physical currency and monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more and Statistics Canada international trade declarations for statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for the SFO treasury function: Low. Canadian federal banking law (Bank Act) requires a Schedule I or II bank charter to accept deposits; most offshore/European Fintech EMIs (e.g., Revolut, Wise, BlackBanx) are neither chartered in Canada nor prohibitively restricted for cross-border remittances but cannot offer insured deposits (CDIC coverage), prime brokerage, or custody-grade clearing. Their utility is limited to low-value spot conversion and correspondent settlement enhancements, with mandatory FINTRAC registration as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) where they operate in Canada. They are structurally unsuitable as the primary clearing and custody rail for a medium-risk SFO under Alberta securities custody expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statutory mandate mandates physical attendance for corporate account opening; however, PCMLTFA client identification rules and bank risk-appetite policies for medium-risk enhanced structures impose a de facto in-person component. Canada's Big Five banks accept hybrid onboarding: an in-person visit to a Calgary or Edmonton business banking centre for the primary dealing officer and beneficial owners, combined with video-enabled KYC interviews (Teams/Zoom) for remote directors. A fully remote electronic onboarding is generally reserved for simple, Canadian-resident-owned operating companies. For an SFO with non-resident settlor or foreign-resident directors, the standard requirement is an in-person branch interview with the account's relationship manager and compliance officer, executed in the presence of the corporate secretary or an authorized agent, plus a notarized certificate of incumbency and physical passport verification (or eKYC via a qualified verification agent).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layered beneficial ownership (trust, holding companies, discretionary beneficiaries) obscuring the ultimate owner(s); banks apply enhanced due diligence above 10% threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified organizational chart; up-to-date Alberta Registry Corporate Access Number (CAN) extract; formal trust deed and deed of appointment (or sanitized extract with settlor, trustee, and named beneficiaries); beneficiary register (where lawfully available); certificate of incumbency; board resolution authorizing account opening and signatory delegation; legal opinion from Alberta counsel confirming the SFO's control architecture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth / source of funds opacity on institutional-scale capital injection (asset sale proceeds, inheritance, offshore holdings).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements of the holding entity; 12–24 months of bank statements showing the provenance of funds; executed sale-and-purchase agreements, share sale agreements, or disposition settlement statements; probate grants, wills, or inheritance receipts; foreign tax returns (T1/T2 equivalents); CRA tax clearance or NoA; letter from an external regulated investment advisor corroborating wealth trajectory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or UBOs with tax residencies in high-risk or FATF-monitored jurisdictions (including offshore financial centres).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport copies (notarized); proof of residency (utility bills, tax assessment); immigration status (visa/work permit) where the individual is in Canada; international corporate and tax profile via CRA Form NR71 or TP matching; negative news/AML screening reports; a professional reference letter from a regulated financial intermediary in the individual's home jurisdiction; enhanced continuous monitoring consent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared investment mandate and transaction counterparty universe (e.g., settlement to countries on the CFPOA advisory lists, crypto exchanges, or high-risk sectors), triggering bank trade surveillance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal Investment Policy Statement (IPS) approved by the family board/trustee; portfolio constraint schedule expressly prohibiting unregulated digital assets and restricted jurisdictions; draft model portfolio or custody confirmation from a Canadian regulated broker-dealer; annual AML attestation and internal control memorandum; engagement letter with an independent family office administrator providing transaction coding for SWIFT purpose codes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocol: (1) foreign entity remits CAD or foreign currency via SWIFT MT103 to the SFO's operational account at a Big Five clearing bank; (2) domestic settlement occurs through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) in real-time; (3) ISO 20022 / SWIFT purpose codes must be populated (e.g., EQUI for equity contributions, INVE for general investment flows, or TRAD for trading settlement) and must exactly match the declared source-of-funds rationale in the bank's onboarding file; (4) supporting documentation (share subscription agreement, Director's Resolution, statement of source of funds, and for shareholder loans, a signed promissory note) must be retained for FATCA/CRS and bank surveillance audits; (5) no exchange control approval is required; funds credited in CAD are freely usable, but amounts over CAD 10,000 will generate FINTRAC reports if moved in physical form, and all electronic wire payments are recorded by FINTRAC's SWIFTR data capture for national threat assessment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103/MT202 for cross-border wires; LVTS for high-value Canadian-dollar domestic transfers; ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System, via EFT) for low-value recurring disbursements; and the emerging Real-Time Rail (RTR) for instant domestic retail payments. Trade-related disbursements are executed by bank-guaranteed Commercial Letters of Credit under ICC UCP 600 rules (advising/confirming bank in the seller's jurisdiction) and by standby LCs (ISP98) for performance guarantees. For listed-securities purchases, settlement flows through CDS (CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc., part of TMX Group) via an approved Canadian custodian; cross-currency settlement of USD/CAD is cleared through the bank's U.S. correspondent network (e.g., RBC's U.S. entity, TD Bank, N.A.). All outbound payments require matching SWIFT purpose codes and an anti-money-laundering screening against OFAC/EU/Canadian sanctions lists in real-time.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards between CAD and USD/EUR/GBP, matching underlying exposure, documentation under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement plus Credit Support Annex (CSA) with the Canadian chartered bank.

Cross-currency swaps for term-matched asset-liability hedging on portfolio investments, governed by the Alberta Securities Commission derivatives framework and reported to an eligible trade repository.
FX options (vanilla calls/puts) on a delta-hedged basis for hedging only, not for speculative accretion, consistent with a conservative SFO investment policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency counterparties (e.g., CNY, KRW) subject to the bank's credit limits and internal risk approval; the SFO qualifies as an 'eligible derivatives party' under NI 93-101 if total financial assets exceed CAD 5 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary of incorporation or the date of the last annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative dissolution possible after 60 days of default notice; fines up to $200 plus costs

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required only for public corporations; optional for private corporations unless required by articles of incorporation or special resolution of shareholders

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual UBO confirmation required in Alberta; annual return must disclose directors, officers and registered office address. Shareholding transfers require immediate update to Register of Members

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined (15% federal Part I general rate plus 8% Alberta general corporate rate) for active business income; 46.67% combined statutory levy before refunds (38.67% federal Part I on aggregate investment income plus 8% Alberta) for a private Canadian-controlled investment holding company such as an SFO
